health.title: Pet Health Gear: Ramps, Cat Grass and DNA Tests
health.description: Dog ramps for senior dogs, cat grass growing kits and dog DNA tests, compared on what each one does and where it falls short.
health.intro: These guides cover health-adjacent gear: ramps that spare an older dog the jump, cat grass for indoor grazers, and DNA tests that answer the breed question. They spell out the limits, and none of it replaces a vet's advice.

supplements.title: Dog and Cat Supplements
supplements.description: Joint, probiotic, fish oil and hairball supplements for dogs and cats, compared on format, ingredients and what each is meant for.
supplements.intro: Supplements come in powders, chews, oils and capsules, and the right format is often the one your pet will actually take. These guides compare supplements by what they are meant for and how they are given, and they say plainly where the evidence is thin. Ask your vet before starting any supplement, especially for a pet on medication.

calming.title: Calming Products for Anxious Dogs and Cats
calming.description: Calming diffusers, treats, anxiety vests and other calming aids for dogs and cats, compared by trigger, format and species.
calming.intro: Storms, travel, a new home and time alone all unsettle pets in different ways. These guides match calming products to the trigger, from plug-in diffusers to treats and vests, and note which ones work only for cats or only for dogs. Results vary from pet to pet, and sudden behavior changes call for a vet visit first.

dental.title: Dog and Cat Dental Care
dental.description: Dental chews, dental treats and water additives for dogs and cats, compared on format, size and how easily they fit into a routine.
dental.intro: Most pets will never sit still for daily brushing, so dental products try to meet them halfway. These guides cover chews, treats and water additives, weighing how easy a product is to use every day against what it is meant to do. None replaces a dental check at the vet.

flea-tick.title: Flea and Tick Prevention for Dogs and Cats
flea-tick.description: Flea and tick treatments for dogs and cats, compared by format, species and how often they need applying.
flea-tick.intro: Flea and tick products come as collars, topical drops, sprays and chews, and the format decides how easy it is to stay on schedule. These guides compare options by species, format and application interval. Your vet is the right call for prescription options and for a pet with health issues.

grooming.title: Dog and Cat Grooming Tools
grooming.description: Dog grooming kits, nail grinders and cat grooming brushes, compared by coat type, noise and how easy they are to use at home.
grooming.intro: Grooming at home saves money only if the tool suits your pet's coat and temperament. These guides cover brushes for different cat coats, nail grinders and dog grooming tools. Along the way, they note what helps a nervous pet get through it.

outdoor.title: Outdoor Dog Gear: Picks for Every Season
outdoor.description: Dog life jackets, pools, sun protection, hot-pavement boots and tie-outs, compared on fit, safety features and how they hold up outside.
outdoor.intro: Outdoor gear has to work on a hot sidewalk, a lake and a long afternoon in the yard. These guides cover dog gear for water, sun, heat and staying put, with the safety features worth paying for called out. Fit matters more than features here.

food.title: Dog and Cat Food: Picks by Life Stage
food.description: Kitten, puppy, senior dog, wet and grain-free cat food compared, plus the label lines that tell you whether a food fits your pet's age.
food.intro: The right food depends on your pet's age before it depends on the brand. These guides cover kittens, puppies, senior dogs and adult cats, starting with the label line that shows which life stage a food is made for. Change foods slowly, and check with your vet before a big switch.

treats.title: Dog and Cat Treats: Picks by Purpose
treats.description: Training treats, freeze-dried bites, lickable cat treats and seasonal picks, compared on ingredients, size and how pets take to them.
treats.intro: A treat does a job, whether that job is rewarding a sit, hiding a pill or filling a stocking. These guides sort dog and cat treats by what you need them for. Treats should stay a small part of the daily diet.

feeding.title: Pet Feeders, Fountains and Slow Bowls
feeding.description: Automatic cat feeders, pet water fountains, slow feeder dog bowls and cat puzzle feeders, compared on capacity, cleaning and pace.
feeding.intro: How a pet eats matters as much as what it eats. These guides cover timed feeders for busy days, fountains for pets who don't drink enough, and bowls and puzzles that slow down a fast eater. How much work the gear takes to keep clean is part of every comparison.

toys.title: Dog and Cat Toys: Picks by Play Style
toys.description: Chew-proof dog toys, interactive puzzles, catnip, tunnels and snuffle mats, sorted by how your pet plays and whether it keeps them busy without you.
toys.intro: A toy that gets ignored after a day costs the same as one that gets played with for a year. These guides sort dog and cat toys by how your pet actually plays: chewing, chasing, sniffing or solving. Look for notes on which toys hold up to a power chewer and which ones keep a pet busy on their own.

collars.title: Dog and Cat Collars: Picks for Fit and Safety
collars.description: Collars for small dogs, night-walk collars and breakaway cat collars, compared on fit, hardware and the safety features worth having.
collars.intro: A collar has to stay on, stay comfortable and carry an ID tag every day. These guides cover collars for small necks, visibility for dark evening walks and breakaway designs that release if a cat gets snagged.

harnesses.title: Dog and Cat Harnesses
harnesses.description: No-pull dog harnesses and cat harness and leash sets, compared on fit, adjustment points and how well they stop a pet from slipping out.
harnesses.intro: A harness spreads pressure across the chest instead of the neck, which suits pullers, small dogs and cats learning to walk outside. These guides cover no-pull designs for dogs and escape-resistant sets for cats. Measuring comes first, since a loose harness is the one a pet backs out of.

training.title: Dog and Cat Training Gear
training.description: Puppy pads, training clickers and deterrents that keep cats off counters and trees, compared on how they fit into everyday training.
training.intro: Training gear works best as a helper for consistent habits, not a replacement for them. These guides cover house-training supplies, clickers for marking good behavior, and deterrents that steer pets away from the places you want kept clear.

litter.title: Cat Litter and Litter Boxes
litter.description: Odor-control litter, litter boxes and self-cleaning litter boxes, compared on smell, dust, cleanup and fit for multi-cat homes.
litter.intro: Most litter box trouble comes down to a mismatch: the wrong litter, the wrong box, or too few boxes for the cats in the house. These guides cover odor-control litters, litter boxes, and automatic boxes that do the scooping for you. They also note what fits a multi-cat home.

scratching.title: Cat Scratchers and Cat Trees
scratching.description: Scratching posts, cardboard scratchers and cat trees for big cats and small spaces, compared on stability, height and how long they last.
scratching.intro: Cats are going to scratch something, so the only choice is where. These guides cover posts, cardboard scratchers and cat trees, judged on the things that decide whether a cat uses them: height, stability and the scratching surface. A scratcher that wobbles gets ignored, and the couch takes the hit.

beds.title: Dog and Cat Beds: Picks for Every Sleeper
beds.description: Beds for large dogs, cooling mats, elevated cots, cat beds and window perches and hammocks, compared on support, washability and fit.
beds.intro: Dogs and cats sleep most of the day, so the bed is the piece of gear they use most. These guides cover big-dog support, beds that run cool, and cats who want the sunniest window in the house. The comparisons come down to fit, cleanup and how well a bed holds its shape.

crates.title: Dog Crates, Playpens and Crate Gear
crates.description: Dog crates, portable playpens and crate pads, compared on size, setup, cleaning and how well they suit a new puppy.
crates.intro: A crate or playpen gives a dog a safe spot of its own and gives you a break. These guides cover wire and soft crates, playpens that fold for travel, and the pads and covers that make a crate comfortable. Get the size right before anything else: a crate that is too big or too small undoes most of its purpose.

carriers.title: Cat and Dog Carriers: Picks for Every Trip
carriers.description: Cat travel carriers, cat backpacks and dog backpack carriers, compared on ventilation, sizing and how they carry over a long walk.
carriers.intro: A carrier your pet hates turns every vet trip into a fight. These guides cover cat travel carriers, bubble-window backpacks and backpack carriers for small dogs.

travel.title: Dog Car Travel Gear
travel.description: Dog car booster seats, car seat covers and travel water bottles, compared on fit, cleanup and keeping a dog settled on the road.
travel.intro: A dog who rides well makes every trip easier, and the right gear does most of that work. These guides cover booster seats for small dogs, seat covers that survive mud and hair, and water bottles for stops along the way.

cleaning.title: Pet Cleaning Gear: Hair, Stains and Odor
cleaning.description: Pet hair removers, stain and odor eliminators and vacuums for pet hair, compared on what they lift, what they leave behind and how much work they take.
cleaning.intro: Living with a dog or cat means hair on the couch and the odd accident on the rug. These guides cover the gear that deals with both, from lint tools and laundry hair catchers to enzyme cleaners and vacuums built for fur. The surfaces each product suits are noted too.

tech.title: Pet Tech: Cameras and GPS Trackers
tech.description: Pet cameras and GPS dog trackers, compared on features and subscription costs.
tech.intro: Pet tech lets you check in on a pet you can't see, whether it's on the couch at home or somewhere past the fence. These guides cover pet cameras and GPS trackers, including the ongoing costs, like subscriptions, that the sticker price leaves out. Battery life and app quality decide most of the experience, so both get a close look.
